one_liner: Single-file SIMD kernel for in-place square float transpose with scaling; 3-6x faster than MKL mkl_simatcopy at N>=64.
what_it_does: Computes A := alpha * A^T in place for a square single-precision matrix with a padded leading dimension. This is the job of the BLAS-extension routine mkl_simatcopy('R','T',...) / cblas_simatcopy. The whole API is one extern "C" function, transpose_inplace_tiled_simd(float* A, uint32_t m, float alpha, uint32_t stride), in transpose_inplace_tiled_simd.cpp. alpha == 1.0f takes an unscaled pure-transpose path. The rest of the repo (main.cpp, utils/) is a benchmark and perf-counter harness.
how_it_is_fast: Two-level cache blocking: 32x32 blocks, each split into 4x4 (SSE/NEON) or 8x8 (AVX2) register tiles. Off-diagonal tile pairs are swapped by loading one tile into a small buffer and doing an in-register unpack/shuffle transpose of each side, with the alpha multiply fused into the same pass so the data is touched only once. Separate loops handle full blocks, edge blocks, edge tiles and the diagonal (the README calls this 'branch-elimination via structured iteration spaces'), so the inner loops carry no bounds checks. The baseline instead calls a general imatcopy routine.
when_to_use: Single-threaded in-place transpose-and-scale of square float matrices from about 64x64 to 2048x2048 on x86 with SSE/AVX2, where the chart shows about 3.1-6.2x over MKL 2025.1 sequential.
Hot loops that call mkl_simatcopy on small or medium square float matrices and only need the transposed, scaled result.
As a readable reference for a fused SIMD 4x4/8x8 in-register transpose to adapt into your own code, after getting the author's permission (no license).
when_not_to_use: Any shipped code: the repo has no LICENSE file, so the code cannot legally be copied or vendored.
Rectangular, out-of-place, double, complex or conjugate transposes: only square float in place is implemented.
Very small matrices (about 1.4x at N=16) or very large ones (m*stride above 2^32 elements overflows its uint32_t index math, by inspection of the source).
Multi-threaded workloads: the kernel is single-threaded and was compared only against single-threaded (sequential) MKL.
ARM: a NEON path and an OpenBLAS cblas_simatcopy comparison exist in code, but no ARM results are published.

integration.dependencies: none for the kernel. The benchmark needs Intel MKL 2025.1 at a hard-coded /opt/intel/oneapi path on x86, or OpenBLAS at /opt/homebrew on ARM; perf counters are Linux only.
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 for the kernel (if constexpr). The project builds as C++20 with clang-17 and CMake 3.8+.
integration.platforms: x86-64 with SSE (AVX2 8x8 tiles only with -DFORCE_AVX2=ON), aarch64 with NEON. Anything else hits '#error Only SSE/AVX2 and NEON are supported'.
integration.thread_safety: not documented. The function keeps no global state (its scratch buffer is on the stack), so concurrent calls on different matrices look safe by inspection.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it covers only mkl_simatcopy with ordering 'R'/'C', trans 'T', rows == cols and lda == ldb. The signature differs, uses uint32_t sizes and has no error handling.

gotchas: The kernel tells the compiler A is 64-byte aligned (__builtin_assume_aligned(A, 64)). Passing an unaligned pointer is undefined behaviour, even though the intrinsics use unaligned loads.

The default build (build_and_run.sh passes -DFORCE_AVX2=OFF) uses 128-bit 4x4 tiles even on AVX2 machines. The llvm-mca analysis shows almost only xmm instructions, so the published numbers are presumably from the SSE path. 8x8 AVX2 tiles must be enabled explicitly.
Reported bandwidth counts only the m(m-1)/2 off-diagonal pairs (2 loads + 2 stores each). The matrix is rewritten before every timed call, so both kernels start from cache-warm data.
The benchmark uses stride = m + 16 floats (one cache line of padding), which avoids power-of-two set conflicts. Unpadded power-of-two strides were not measured.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling in this category does in-place transposes; the others (Eigen, BLASFEO, the GEMM kernels) solve different problems. The real choice is against the baseline: use this over mkl_simatcopy or cblas_simatcopy only for single-threaded, square, float, in-place transpose-scale at N>=64, and only if the license question is settled.
verified_claims_summary: utils/time_kernel.cpp times the kernel against mkl_simatcopy('R','T') from MKL 2025.1 linked sequential, single-threaded and pinned to CPU 0 on an i7-14700K at 5.5 GHz. It was built with clang-17 -O3 -march=native -ffast-math, and a final element-by-element check compares the two results. Percentile bandwidth (p10/p50/p90) over power-of-two sizes gives about 1.4x at N=16, 2.7x at N=32, 3.1-3.3x at N=64-256 and 4.4-6.2x at N=512-2048, with values read from a chart image.
status_note: Hobby/portfolio project (1 star, last commit 2026-01-10) with no license, so it is reference-only: the technique is worth studying, but the code cannot be copied without the author's permission.
